_note: Filipino. The 134 example sentences and the nine explanations that still
carried the English headword, written out in Filipino.
This is the first of the remaining seventeen in Latin script, and so the
first that could have needed a long english_ok - Filipino has taken both
Spanish and English wholesale, and half this lexicon is exactly the register
that gets taken. It needed none, and the reason is a spelling convention
rather than a vocabulary one: Filipino respells what it borrows to its own
orthography, so the loan is teodisiya and metonimya and neolohismo and
tautolohiya and pedante, never the English form. That is the Italian answer
(morphology makes the loan local) arriving through spelling instead.
Where a plainer Tagalog word existed it was reached for first, per the rule
since French, and it is usually the better word as well as the safer one:
pietistic is mapagbanal-banalan, paroxysm is silakbo, dotage is
pagkaulyanin, canaille is gusgusing madla, peculation is pangungurakot,
cant is pakitang-taong usapan, plumb-line is pisi't tingga.
mortised is the row worth naming. Filipino carpentry has uka at dila - the
hole and the tongue - so the sentence needed neither the English joint name
nor an exemption. It matters because `mortise` is one of the four standalone
words find_unsaid_english.py turned up: had it been left, segmentTranslation
would have cut it out and handed it to the English voice.
mathesis was reworded to pangkalahatang agham ng kaalaman rather than
exempted - Filipino would otherwise have taken the Latin unchanged.
